description: Figure 2 illustrates the taxonomy of medical ethics, visually representing the relationship between core principles and more detailed categories. The chart is composed of two concentric circles, divided into segments. The inner circle contains four slices, representing the four pillar principles: Respect for Autonomy (light gray, approximately 25%), Beneficence (dark gray, approximately 25%), Non-Maleficence (white, approximately 25%), and Justice (black, approximately 25%). The outer circle is divided into 26 slices, representing categories clustered from 256 detailed principles; these slices vary in size but are not individually labeled with percentages. A legend associates colors with the four pillar principles, and the chart does not include percentage labels within the slices or any visually emphasized segments. The slices in the outer circle appear to be arranged in a non-specific order, without a clear visual pattern of ascending or descending size.
